description: Counts of how Americans take turns when they talk at work or across a counter: turn length, short-turn share, question rate, reaction tokens, turn openers and hedges. Counts and one- to three-word tokens only; no line from the corpus ships.

source.document: Santa Barbara Corpus of Spoken American English, Parts 1 to 4
source.publisher: University of California, Santa Barbara, Department of Linguistics

coverage: The 14 recordings the corpus describes as work or service talk: a lawyer preparing witnesses, board members, bank loan officers, an audio store sale, a veterinary office, an air traffic tower, a heating sales call, aquarium training, a dietitian and an orthopedist with patients, a small claims court, a ranch bill of sale, a judo class, and two coworkers on a break. Recordings 8, 10, 14, 16, 18, 22, 29, 39, 41, 46, 53, 56, 57 and 60.

mining.turnRule: A turn is the run of transcript lines by one speaker until another speaker begins.
mining.selection: Chosen from each recording's own description on the corpus page; family, friends, classroom and public talk are left out.
